newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB CEO SAYS FORECAST SETS FLOOR.
newsitem.headline: ABB CEO SAYS FORECAST SETS FLOOR.

text.p: Goran Lindahl, chief executive of ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said the company's forecast for 1997 set a floor for profits and opened up the possibility that net profit could be higher than 1996's $1.233 billion.
"I can confirm that we have set a floor and we are sticking with that floor," Lindahl told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Earlier today ABB said in its half-year report that net income for the full year of 1997 is expected to reach at least the same level as 1996.
"At least means that we have given a leeway so it (profit) could be above that," Lindahl said, commenting on the forecast.
"In light of a now better backlog, growing orders and that the business environment does not get worse, then it is encouraging for the future," Lindahl added.
ABB first issued the same forecast at its annual news conference in February and restated it when first quarter results were released in April.
